### Sources

The first-month full health pass rechecked all 21 source families maintained before today's change at the capability each family actually promises. Discovery-only families were rechecked against representative current first-party discovery routes and their existing rights/access boundary; direct-TXT families were rechecked against their stable source/snapshot identity and transport/resource boundary; WebNR Originals remains the internal direct-TXT baseline. The result is 21 of 21 retained, zero removals, zero downgrades, and zero failure-driven replacements. No healthy discovery source was falsely upgraded into a crawler or synchronization adapter merely because its public page remained reachable.

The daily new-candidate program additionally screened five previously untracked source families: the DBNL dataset, Project Laurens Jansz. Coster, Victorian Women Writers Project, Wright American Fiction 1851–1875, and Biblioteca Italiana. At least three received full bounded capability audits; the operating research covered all five deeply enough to classify the next action. DBNL is the strongest next public-domain direct-TXT/TEI pilot candidate but must be restricted to an evidenced public-domain subset. VWWP is a strong TEI candidate whose electronic-text header and attribution boundary must survive conversion. Biblioteca Italiana and Wright remain deferred until current reuse-license and stable-endpoint/quality boundaries are sufficiently explicit. Coster is best approached through a stable archival route because the legacy project is no longer updated.

Pull request #139 also promoted yesterday's strongest audited candidate, CLiGS Textbox, into a real passing integration. `CLiGS Textbox Spanish-American TXT Starter` contains exactly three plain-text items from `Collection of 19th Century Spanish-American Novels (1880-1916)`: `nh0003` / *Laucha*, `nh0004` / *Inca*, and `nh0011` / *Rumbo*. Every raw URL is pinned to upstream `cligs/textbox` commit `1b91e940475c8a7e866457a3953fed5edb0a29f1`; the selected files are each below 1 MiB. The collection states that the authors' copyright has expired and publishes the collection under CC BY 4.0 with a citation request. WebNR preserves that provenance/attribution boundary and does not generalize it to unrelated CLiGS collections.

The CLiGS runtime remains bounded: adding the source fetches only WebNR's small YAML index; a reader explicitly selecting one work uses the existing browser URL-import path to request that one commit-pinned `raw.githubusercontent.com` TXT. There is no background polling, catalog crawl, bulk clone, proxy, credential/cookie use, account automation, JavaScript execution, archive extraction, or silent fallback to an unreviewed mirror. The maintained set therefore increases from 21 to 22 source families after #139 without widening existing source contracts.
